chunks: When the two forces drew within seeing distance of each other, the people of Moses said: 'We shall certainly be overtaken.'

key_terms.الْجَمْعَانِ: the two armies / the two forces
key_terms.تَرَاءَى: saw each other / became visible to one another

ai.seo_question: What did the people of Moses say when they saw the Egyptian army approaching?
ai.summary: In this verse from Surah Ash-Shu'ara, the Israelites' exclamation 'Indeed, we are overtaken' reflects their momentary loss of faith despite witnessing the parting of the sea, a key moment of psychological tension before Musa's reassurance. Shia exegetes often highlight this as a test of *yaqin* (certainty), illustrating that even the righteous may experience doubt when the divine promise seems delayed. This narrative underscores the transition from physical salvation to spiritual trial, emphasizing reliance on Allah amidst visible circumstances.
